X.note: The terrain relief is attractive and the labels are clean. The route is weak: three short, identical streaks fan out from Ulsan into open sea with no destinations, arrowheads or scale. 'to buyers abroad' points at a single dot, so it reads as one vague spot and not a route. The 'South Korea' label sits on random inland mountains and nothing marks the country as a whole. The source line is small and low-contrast, and the caption is plain white on dark. The map is zoomed so far in that the viewer has no context for where this is.

Y.note: The globe render is rich and broadcast-quality. Texas is highlighted in orange, so the place is clear within a second. The callout and caption are large and legible. The callout text is slightly small on a phone, and the source line is tiny and low-contrast. The 'As of 12 Oct 2026' tag is a useful honesty cue. It shows a state highlight and not a movement or route, so it only loosely fits 'route across a region'. The callout box covers part of the Midwest and Gulf, though this does not hurt understanding.

why: Y shows its subject (Texas) instantly with a premium globe render and legible, well-placed text, whereas X's vague, unlabeled export lines and tight crop leave the viewer unsure what the route shows.
top_fix_for_weaker: Draw one clear, thick route from Ulsan out to named destinations (e.g. Rotterdam, Houston) with arrowheads and labels. Zoom out enough to show the Korean peninsula and its neighbors, outline South Korea, and raise the contrast and size of the source line.
